_provenance.script: regrade of recorded trials via tasks/*/scripts/regrade.sh
_provenance.note: Local Docker, --network none, 8 CPU. Both verifiers are gpus=0 in production ([verifier.environment] in task.toml), so these are representative rather than an optimistic local figure.

budget_note: test.sh runs the grader under `timeout 3000`; task.toml allows 3600s.

qa-sft-adapt.note: ~7,200 log-likelihood forwards through a 135M causal LM at <=160 tokens, plus check_closer_to_base loading submission + base + sibling.

pref-reward-model.note: ~7,900 forwards through an 82M encoder at <=256 tokens. The 1,933s recorded in posttrain/RESULTS.md was for two eval sets; this is one.

conclusion: Neither verifier is near its timeout. The concern was that qa -- three eval sets through a larger model -- would be worse than pref's recorded 1,933s for two. It is 4.5x faster per eval set, so the extrapolation from pref was wrong.
